# /contract

`/contract` is the truth-claim primitive for agent-driven work. Declare what must hold,
iterate until genuinely satisfied, spawn children when sub-work emerges. One ledger row
per event; the ledger is the only memory. **SKILL.md is the canonical reference** — this
file is a derived view.

## Install

The skill lives at `~/.claude/skills/contract/`. First-use setup:

```bash
# verify the CLI is on the right path and the substrate is sane
bash ~/.claude/skills/contract/scripts/contract self
bash ~/.claude/skills/contract/scripts/skill-self-test.sh
```

If both exit 0, the substrate is live. The ledger writes to
`~/.contracts/contracts.jsonl` (set `CONTRACTS_STORE` to scope per-project).

## When to invoke

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| "contract this" / "X must always hold" | `contract declare "<plan>" --action "<check>"` |
| "build and run this" | `contract build "<plan>" --action "<check>"` |
| "solve until done" | `contract solve "<plan>" --action "<check>"` |
| "this is a sub-problem of Y" | `contract spawn <parent-id> "<plan>" --action "<check>"` |
| "keep building / drill to completion / finish without asking" | `contract drive <organ-id>` |
| "what contracts exist" | `contract list` or `contract status [<id>]` |
| "is this a recurring pattern?" | `contract search` |
| "convert past patterns" / "don't lose this in the refactor" | `contract import <source>` |

On any invocation: read `ledgers/contracts.jsonl` — it is the only truth. The full verb list (38+) is discoverable via `contract self`; the table above is the load-bearing front door (Ψ2, working-memory cap).

## Substrate principle

Substrate enables; it does not prescribe. Scripts emit evidence only. The agent
renders every verdict in-thread. A contract that auto-satisfies is a tautology.
